    Run a GROBID service on a single file

    grobid_process_file.Rd

    Sends a file (or, for the "processCitationList" service, the possibility of using a vector of raw text citations) to the GROBID API and returns the result as raw (XML/TEI) or parsed. Supports the four main GROBID services: full text extraction, header metadata extraction, bibliographic reference extraction, and parsing of raw text citation lists.

    If no GROBID server is active (Docker or remote), the function attempts to automatically start/validate the connection via grobid_docker_start() or grobid_remote_connect() before sending the request (see argument .ensure_server).

    Usage

    grobid_process_file(
  file,
  service = "processFulltextDocument",
  params = list(),
  output_dir = NULL,
  output_format = "parsed",
  mode = NULL,
  model_type = .checkrefr_env$grobid_model_type,
  verbose = TRUE,
  .ensure_server = TRUE,
  user_agent = NULL
)

    Arguments

    file

    character - Full path to the file to process. PDF files are expected for all services except "processCitationList" which expects a .txt file (one citation per line). For this service only, file can also be a vector of raw text citations (each element being a citation).

    service

    character Name of the GROBID service to use. Accepted values:

    • "processFulltextDocument" - full text extraction

    • "processHeaderDocument" - header metadata extraction (title, authors, abstract, affiliations...)

    • "processReferences" - bibliographic reference extraction

    • "processCitationList" - parsing of citations from a text file or a vector of raw citations (one citation per line)

    Default: "processFulltextDocument". See the full list of available services in the official GROBID documentation.

    params

    list Additional parameters passed to the HTTP form of the GROBID API. Common examples:

    • consolidateHeader = 1 - metadata enrichment via Crossref

    • consolidateCitations = 1 - reference enrichment via Crossref

    • includeRawCitations = 1 - include raw citations in the response

    These parameters correspond to the options accepted by the GROBID endpoints. For an exhaustive list, see the official API documentation. By default the argument is an empty list: list().

    output_dir

    character or NULL. If provided, the XML result is saved in this folder under the name {file_name}.tei.xml (or citations.tei.xml if file is a citation vector). The folder is created automatically if it does not exist. In this case, the function returns the path of the saved file (invisible). If NULL, the result is returned directly. Default: NULL.

    output_format

    character Format of the result returned when output_dir = NULL:

    • "raw" - raw XML/TEI string

    • "parsed" - structured result (tibble)

    Default: "parsed".

    mode

    character or NULL. Connection mode to the GROBID server: "docker" or "remote". If NULL, the function uses the configuration stored in the package's internal environment (default "docker" if not configured). Default: NULL. Note on internal configuration: To persistently modify the mode or other global variables (port, timeout, etc.) for your R session, use the function checkrefr_set_defaults.

    model_type

    character or NA. GROBID model variant to use for bibliographic citation extraction. Two values are possible:

    • "crf" - model based solely on a CRF (Conditional Random Field). Faster, but generally less accurate than the "full" model.

    • "full" - model combining CRF and a neural (deep learning) model. More accurate, but slower and more resource intensive.

    This parameter corresponds to the model.name / citation configuration in GROBID's YAML config file (see the official documentation for details HERE). If NA (default value), in docker mode the sensible default model is used, see the GROBID dockerHub documentation for details or use the function grobid_docker_list_versions(). In remote mode a crf model is used by default. Default: .checkrefr_env$grobid_model_type, i.e. NA.

    verbose

    logical If TRUE, displays progress messages in the console. Default: TRUE.

    .ensure_server

    logical If TRUE, checks and automatically starts the GROBID server (Docker or remote) before running the request. Disable (FALSE) only when the server availability has already been validated upstream (e.g. repeated calls from grobid_process_files()). Default: TRUE.

    user_agent

    character or NULL. Custom User-Agent string to send with the HTTP request to the GROBID API. Default: NULL.

    Value

    The return type depends on the arguments:

    • output_dir provided -> path of the saved .tei.xml file (invisible(character))

    • output_format = "raw" -> character containing the XML/TEI

    • output_format = "parsed" -> tibble or data.frame depending on the service, with a source_file column

    • On failure -> invisible(NA_character_) with a warning

    References

    Official GROBID API documentation: https://grobid.readthedocs.io/en/latest/Grobid-service/

    See also

    grobid_process_files(), grobid_docker_start(), grobid_remote_connect(), parse_fulltext(), parse_header(), parse_references(), parse_citation_list(),checkrefr_set_defaults()

    Examples

    if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Example of a full workflow using the package's example files

# 1. Retrieve an example PDF provided with the package
pdf_file <- system.file("extdata", package = "CheckrefR") |>
  list.files(pattern = "\\.pdf$", full.names = TRUE) |>
  (\(x) x[1])()

# 2. Start the GROBID server in Docker mode (optional)
grobid_docker_start()

# 3. Full text extraction, parsed result
fulltext <- grobid_process_file(
  file          = pdf_file,
  service       = "processFulltextDocument",
  params        = list(consolidateHeader = 1),
  output_format = "parsed"
)

# 4. Extraction of bibliographic references from the same document
refs <- grobid_process_file(
  file          = pdf_file,
  service       = "processReferences",
  params        = list(consolidateHeader = 1),
  output_format = "parsed"
)

# 5. Processing a raw citations file (.txt) provided as an example
txt_file <- system.file("extdata", package = "CheckrefR") |>
  list.files(pattern = "\\.txt$", full.names = TRUE) |>
  (\(x) x[1])()

citations_parsed <- grobid_process_file(
  file          = txt_file,
  service       = "processCitationList",
  params        = list(consolidateHeader = 1),
  output_format = "parsed"
)

# 6. Cleanly stop the Docker container
grobid_docker_stop()
} # }
